title: DataShare VCTK 0.92 fixtures (10 train speakers p225-p234, held-out p236/p237/p238), cached as .npz
content:
The original notebook's data. build_split() pulls selected speakers' FLACs out of the Edinburgh DataShare
VCTK-Corpus-0.92.zip (fetch_vctk over HTTP ranges, ~11 GB archive) and caches each split as an .npz. The
FULL preset trains on 10 speakers p225-p234 and holds out p236, p237, p238. The held-out cache
(test_FULL.npz in the notes) is the "DataShare" evaluation set used by every Mac-side local evaluation
(4 Sep lambda frontier, 8 Sep sampler analysis, wide-context test). Per TODO.md the DataShare URL no
longer serves the archive, and the same checkpoint measures a deeper high-band deficit on the Hub route
than on this cache for the same speakers, with the provenance unresolved (see two-test-set-discrepancy).

extraction.evidence: build_notebook.py: FULL Config (train_speakers p225-p234, test_speakers p236-p238), VCTK_URL, fetch_vctk(), build_split(); TODO.md 'Resolve the two-test-set discrepancy' and '403' items

title: Full VCTK mic1 corpus from the HF Hub (sanchit-gandhi/vctk), 39,639 utterances, 37.32 h
content:
The training corpus for every run from 4 Sep onward (4 Sep lambda frontier, 8 Sep OV2 sampler, OV3_fast,
OV50): VCTK mic1 from the Hugging Face dataset sanchit-gandhi/vctk, 48 kHz, peak-normalised to 0.95,
downsampled by R = 4 to 12 kHz inputs. The OV50 manifest records n = 39639 utterances and 37.32 hours,
with p236/p237/p238 held out (1285 test utterances) and 2961 paper-split test utterances; the OV50 batch
stream is fingerprinted by a corpus digest so every VM trains on the identical corpus.

extraction.evidence: overnight3/results_OV50/manifest.json fields repo, n, hours, test_speakers, n_test_utts, n_paper_test, g3.corpus; loader in overnight/cell1_corpus.py

title: Held-out evaluation splits on the Hub corpus - EVAL12, ours120 (p236-p238) and paper100 (id >= 350)
content:
Speaker-disjoint evaluation sets cut from the Hub corpus. EVAL12 = test_utts[:12] (first 12 Hub
utterances of p236-p238; the "Hub" set in the 8 Sep note and the EVAL12 of OV3_fast/OV50); ours120 = all
p236-p238 test utterances; paper100 = 100 utterances spread over paper_test_utts, LISA's own held-out
split (the speaker-id threshold is set in overnight/cell1_corpus.py). Every number in the repo after 4 Sep names one of these or the DataShare cache, because the same
checkpoint measures differently on them.

extraction.evidence: overnight2/c3_eval.py lines defining EVAL12 and PAPER100, and the eval12 / ours120 / paper100 calls to ensemble_eval; speaker roles (OUR_TEST, PAPER_TEST_MIN = 350) in overnight/cell1_corpus.py

title: Audit fixtures - a few VCTK 0.92 utterances per speaker pulled by HTTP range from DataShare
content:
audit/vctk_fixtures.py reads only the requested members of the 11 GB VCTK 0.92 archive over HTTP range

extraction.evidence: audit/vctk_fixtures.py module docstring, PAPER_TEST / OUR_TEST constants, RangeFile and fetch()

title: NU-Wave 2 / FLowHigh test speakers (p360-p364, p374, p376, s5), files spread through each script
content:
The evaluation set for the released-SOTA audit. sota/fetch_wide.py takes per_speaker files (default 30)
evenly spaced through each speaker's sorted list for the eight NU-Wave 2 / FLowHigh test speakers,
because audit/vctk_fixtures.fetch() takes each speaker's first files and VCTK's first ~24 prompts are the
same sentences for every speaker. Stored in lisa_rtm_cache/audit_wide/ so earlier audit numbers stay
untouched.

extraction.evidence: sota/fetch_wide.py docstring and SPEAKERS constant

title: LISA reimplementation (conv encoder + 5-layer ReLU MLP local implicit decoder) and core metrics
content:
build_notebook.py generates lisa_rtm.ipynb and holds the reimplementation of LISA (Kim et al., ICASSP
2022, ~89k params): LISAEncoder (1-D convs), LISADecoder (MLP on [coord, z(i-1), z(i), z(i+1)]),
MultiScaleSTFTLoss over three scales, and the shared metric definitions snr_db, lsd_db,
band_energy_ratio (with frame_mask), crps_ensemble, pit_ranks, spread_skill. Config sets lambda_spec =
1e-3 (the official code's spec_coeff), Adam lr 1e-3 halved at 0.2/0.4/0.5/0.6/0.7/0.8 of steps,
grad_clip 1e-3; FULL preset batch 16, 20000 steps. Every later script (overnight*, audit/boot.py,
sota/score.py) execs these cells for its model and metric definitions.

extraction.evidence: build_notebook.py classes LISAEncoder/LISADecoder/LISA/MultiScaleSTFTLoss, metric defs snr_db..spread_skill, FULL Config

title: Post-hoc optimal-transport ladder T0-T4 and stochastic rung S on high-band log-magnitude
content:
lisa_rtm.ipynb (generated by build_notebook.py) fits post-hoc maps from the model's high-band
log-magnitude distribution to the truth's: T0 identity, T1 per-bin quantile map (exact 1-D OT), T2
Bures-Wasserstein (diag/block), T3 conditional location-scale on frame covariates, T4 McCann
interpolation (1-lambda) Id + lambda T, and S, noise pushed through a conditional map (the only rung that
produces samples). Includes closed-form OT unit tests run before data, and adversarial controls in the
results table: shaped noise, a deliberately mis-specified T1, and a frame shuffle.

extraction.evidence: lisa_rtm.ipynb sections 5 and 10-12 (QuantileMap, BuresMap, ConditionalMap, Interpolated, controls); source in build_notebook.py

title: LISAS - LISA with 8 Gaussian input channels trained under the two-draw energy score
content:
overnight2/c1_model.py defines LISAS (LISA plus N_NOISE = 8 Gaussian channels at the encoder input;
eps = 0 recovers LISA exactly), the training objectives (det, det_split, es_marg, es_slice, es_wave) with
the two-draw energy score ES = (d(y,y1)+d(y,y2))/2 - d(y1,y2)/2, the distances d_wave/d_logmag/d_sliced,
HostCorpus, the paired trainer train_ov2, and load_arm. load_arm sets tau = 0 iff ck["arm"][0]
startswith "det", which silently mis-reads checkpoints whose arm field is a string (found and worked
around for OV50 by fast/convert_ckpt.py). sampler/build_sampler_notebook.py packages the same recipe as
the self-contained Colab deliverable.

extraction.evidence: overnight2/c1_model.py header comment (objectives), class LISAS, arm_loss, train_ov2, load_arm

title: Coherent fraction, kappa, predictability spectrum rho(f) and deterministic SNR bound
content:
overnight2/analysis_local.py is the independent CPU analysis that computes, per arm, the coherent
fraction Re<Y,P>/<Y,Y> per high-band third octave (the predictable fraction), kappa = Re<Y,P>/<P,P>,
the energy-based predictable fraction bias-corrected for an M-draw mean, the predictability spectrum rho,
the deterministic SNR bound implied by rho, plus CRPS / sliced CRPS / PIT. It execs the notebook's
definition cells and reads the DataShare test cache. The same coherent() estimator is copied into
overnight3/e4_eval.py and reused by sota/score.py.

extraction.evidence: overnight2/analysis_local.py docstring, band_cross() docstring, rho / snr_bound_db / predictable_hb_fraction block

title: OV3 model additions - LISASD decoder noise, ERB-band distance d_erb, logmean ensemble readout
content:
overnight3/e1_model.py extends c1_model.py: LISASD adds N_DEC = 4 Gaussian channels per output sample at
the decoder input; es_erb / es_marg_erb add an L1 distance on log ERB-band energies (32 bands, three STFT
scales), the space ViSQOL's audio-mode neurogram lives in; es_ged and es_split variants; and
logmag_ensemble_readout (mean of log|STFT| over M draws, phase of draw 0, baseband passed through). Used
by OV3_fast, OV50 (via ArmStack in overnight3/e2b_fast.py) and the SOTA scorer.

extraction.evidence: overnight3/e1_model.py header comment, class LISASD, erb_filterbank/d_erb, logmag_ensemble_readout

title: e4_eval.py - EVAL12 evaluation (CRPS, PIT, coherence, readouts, passthrough, floor/ceiling)
content:
overnight3/e4_eval.py evaluates every OV3/OV50 arm on EVAL12: one draw and a 16-draw ensemble (CRPS,
sliced CRPS on 32 fixed directions, PIT, spread-skill, ensemble-mean metrics, coherent fraction and
kappa), the logmean16 / logmean4 readouts, every condition again with baseband passthrough, and the
model-independent floor (passthrough + empty high band) and ceiling (passthrough + true high band) rows.
It loads checkpoints through c1_model's load_arm.

extraction.evidence: overnight3/e4_eval.py header comment, coherent(), passthrough(), floor_ceiling(), load_ov3()

title: LSD + ViSQOL (speech 16 kHz and audio 48 kHz) + PESQ evaluation of every condition
content:
overnight2/c6_visqol_eval.py judges every 8 Sep condition with the user's evaluation.py: ViSQOL speech
mode at 16 kHz (which after resampling sees only 6-8 kHz of the reconstructed 6-24 kHz band), ViSQOL
audio mode at 48 kHz (sees the whole band), and wideband PESQ, keeping per-utterance values for paired
comparisons. overnight3/e5_visqol.py reuses the same evaluation.py call path for OV3 and OV50.

extraction.evidence: overnight2/c6_visqol_eval.py header comment; overnight3/e5_visqol.py header ('same call path as overnight2/c6_visqol_eval.py')

title: OV50 one-arm-per-process resumable trainer and the eight-arm run contract
content:
fast/train_arm.py trains one arm per process, resumably, on a staged corpus, exec'ing ArmStack from
overnight3/e2b_fast.py verbatim as the numerical contract (energy-score estimator, distances, per-arm
clip, sub-pixel decoder) and owning only the loop, because train_ov3_fast cannot resume. fast/run_contract.py
fixes BATCH_TAG / VAL_TAG so all eight arms on eight VMs draw identical batches, guarded by a cross-machine
digest.

extraction.evidence: fast/train_arm.py docstring 'REUSE THE MATH, OWN THE LOOP'; fast/run_contract.py docstring

title: audit/lisa_paper_protocol.py - LISA's own resampler, SNR and LSD reimplemented, no model
content:
Reimplements torchaudio 0.6.0's kaldi.resample_waveform (the only resampler in ml-postech/LISA) and
LISA's utils.calc_snr / compute_log_distortion from source, applies eval_lisa.py's chunking, and reports:
the response of Resample(48000, 48000) on the ground truth, the protocol's ceiling (perfect low band,
empty high band) and where naive sits, the variance created by the `if ii == 3` single-batch evaluation,
LISA's LSD against the conventional one, and how much of their LSD is pinned at its epsilon floor. By
design it depends on nothing in this repo's model code.

extraction.evidence: audit/lisa_paper_protocol.py module docstring items 1-5; audit/README.md last paragraph

title: sota/score.py - one scorer for released BWE checkpoints and our arms
content:
Scores every model's saved draws on one set of utterances with one scorer: levels (LSD in two bases,
per-third-octave deficit, broadband deficit, loud/mid/quiet gated deficit), SNR vs the empty-band
ceiling, coherent fraction and kappa (e4_eval.coherent), CRPS and fair CRPS, PIT tails, spread-skill,
the SNR gap and the independent-draw gap, corr_err, and ViSQOL/PESQ. Metric definitions come from the
notebook via audit.boot, so columns match the OV50 datasheet. Each draw is gain-matched below 5.5 kHz.

extraction.evidence: sota/score.py module docstring (INPUT, GAIN, CONDITIONS, COLUMNS AND IDEALS)

title: Original repro at lambda_spec = 1.0 - right magnitudes, random phase, SNR -5.8 dB
content:
LISA reimplementation trained 20k steps on the DataShare fixtures (10 speakers) with the multi-scale
STFT term at lambda = 1.0, 1000x the official code's 1e-3. The spectral term was 92 % of the loss and the
waveform L1 rose from 0.0557 to 0.0836. Held-out SNR -5.77 dB (worse than silence) while
prediction-magnitude + target-phase resynthesis scored +15.69 dB: correct spectrogram, random waveform.
Band-energy gates could not see it; SNR could.
hypothesis: A deterministic loss on a one-to-many problem makes the high band regress to the conditional mean (H1); the run was the first test of the repro.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-01-eval-audit-and-objective.md §2.1-2.4 tables (same-code-path audit, phase swap, loss terms)

title: Retrain at lambda = 1e-3 - phase fixed, model becomes a sinc interpolator, HB deficit -19.55 dB
content:
Same 0.54 h DataShare training set, lambda_spec = 1e-3, MultiStepLR, 20k steps on an A100. Phase is now
correct but the high band collapses: SNR 18.13 dB vs naive 18.16 (gate 2a fails by 0.03 dB), HB deficit
-19.55 dB, LSD 1.609 (worse than the broken lambda=1.0 model's 1.36). The model emits nothing above 6 kHz;
regression to the conditional median observed directly. Paper reports 24.16 dB.
hypothesis: Matching the official lambda = 1e-3 fixes the waveform and reproduces LISA's SNR.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-01-eval-audit-and-objective.md §2.7 (§9 block) and §3

title: Transport ladder on the lambda=1e-3 model - T1 'wins' HB-LSD but the mis-specified control wins too
content:
Ladder run on the degenerate lambda=1e-3 source (12 held-out DataShare utterances). T1 quantile moved
HB-LSD 1.846 -> 1.226, but the deliberately mis-specified T1 control also improved it to 1.370 because T0
sits on the epsilon floor above 6 kHz, so HB-LSD rewards any energy injection. CRPS deterministic 1.352
-> stochastic rung 1.134. Declared pipeline evidence only; "do not quote".
hypothesis: Transport maps on low-order high-band statistics correct the deficit (H2); only the stochastic rung moves a proper score (H3).

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-01-eval-audit-and-objective.md §2.8 ladder table and §4 rows H2/H3

title: 4 Sep lambda frontier on the 37.3 h Hub corpus - lambda=1e-2 gives a muffled-but-coherent source
content:
Four paired arms on identical batches (batch 64, 1 s chunks, 36,000 steps = 17.1 epochs, A100): ReLU
decoder at lambda 1e-3 / 1e-2 / 1e-1 plus a Fourier-feature control. On the DataShare cache (36 utts)
the HB deficit is monotone in lambda: -17.42 / -4.52 / -2.35 dB, with SNR 19.16 / 18.37 / 17.69 vs naive
19.20 and LSD 1.546 / 0.962 / 0.948. On paper100 relu_l1e-2 scores LSD 0.865 vs the paper's 0.81. No arm
beats naive upsampling; no generalisation gap (bias-limited). The same checkpoint measures -4.5 dB on the
DataShare cache and -10.0 dB on the 120 Hub utterances, so every deficit must name its set.
hypothesis: H1': the deficit is large enough to matter at paper scale; a lambda exists where SNR > naive and the high band is structured but under-energetic.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-04-overnight-lambda-frontier.md §0 run table, §1 local table and §1.0 all-splits table (also overnight/table_allsplits.md, overnight/local_eval_XL4.json)

title: Fourier-feature decoder control - ReLU spectral bias is not the cause (0.6 dB on a 17 dB hole)
content:
Same encoder, latents, loss (lambda 1e-3), batches and seed as relu_l1e-3; only the decoder sees
[c, sin(pi k c), cos(pi k c)] for k = 1..6. DataShare cache: deficit -16.84 vs -17.42 dB, LSD 1.486 vs
1.546, SNR identical. Fourier features do not rescue the high band; over-smoothing comes from objective
and data, not decoder spectral bias. Struck from the notebook's open list.
hypothesis: LISA's ReLU MLP decoder has spectral bias that is a second, architectural cause of over-smoothing.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-04-overnight-lambda-frontier.md §1.3 and §1 table rows ff_l1e-3 / relu_l1e-3

title: Transport ladder on the coherent lambda=1e-2 source - deterministic rungs buy 1.7 %, S buys 21.3 % CRPS
content:
The ladder rerun on relu_l1e-2 (deficit -13.2 dB on this eval set) next to the degenerate relu_l1e-3.
Best rung T1 moves HB-LSD 1.057 -> 1.039 (-1.7 %) for -0.41 dB SNR, versus -42 % on the degenerate
source; the mis-specified T1 control now hurts (1.167 vs T0 1.057), confirming the earlier 'win' was
energy inflation. The stochastic rung S still cuts CRPS 0.957 -> 0.753 (-21.3 %). H2 (deterministic
transport) largely fails on an honest source; H3 supported.
hypothesis: On a coherent, under-energetic source, deterministic transport maps (T1-T3) correct the deficit; only the stochastic rung moves a proper score.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-04-overnight-lambda-frontier.md §2.5 table and §3 rows H2/H3

title: 8 Sep OV2 - LISA trained under the energy score is a sampler; CRPS -43 % (Hub), -32 % (DataShare)
content:
Five arms on identical batches, 38,000 steps of batch 32 x 1 s (9.1 epochs of the Hub corpus). es_marg
(energy score, d = L1 wave + 1e-2 L1 log|STFT|) cuts high-band log-magnitude CRPS 1.015 -> 0.583 vs det
on Hub EVAL12 (-43 %) and 1.011 -> 0.686 on DataShare (-32 %), at zero inference cost. Its ensemble mean
is a better point predictor: SNR 18.90 vs 18.86 (Hub) and 18.78 vs 18.35 (DataShare). Single draw has no
deficit on DataShare (+0.6 dB) but is -7.9 dB in-distribution on Hub (under-dispersed in energy at 9
epochs). Latency 1.51 ms per second of audio on an A100, 16.5 ms on an Apple M4 CPU.
hypothesis: If the network itself is trained as the transport map under a strictly proper score, it becomes a calibrated conditional sampler at zero inference cost; (1) its ensemble mean has det's deficit; (2) a single draw has no deficit.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-08-network-as-transport-map.md §1.1 both tables (rows det, es_marg), §1.2, §3 latency table

title: 8 Sep alternative arms - det_split, es_wave and es_slice all lose to es_marg
content:
det_split (L1 on the low-passed waveform + MS-STFT, the practitioner's deterministic fix) restores energy
(DataShare deficit -2.3 dB) with kappa 0.03 and moves CRPS only 4 %: energy without information.
es_wave (waveform-only energy score) gets energy right (-0.6 dB DataShare) and structure wrong: LSD 1.32
vs 1.03, cross-bin correlation error 1.75 vs 0.62. es_slice (sliced score, proper for the joint law of a
frame) converged slower and was under-dispersed (PIT top bin 41 % on Hub), CRPS 0.782 vs 0.583 on Hub.
hypothesis: A low-band-only waveform term, a waveform-only score, or a joint (sliced) score would do as well as or better than the marginal log-magnitude energy score.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-08-network-as-transport-map.md §1.1 tables (rows det_split, es_slice, es_wave) and §1.2 paragraphs 'geometry of the score' and 'band-split fix'

title: The band above 6 kHz is incoherent - coherent fraction <= 2 %, deterministic ceiling 0.3 dB above naive
content:
Cross-power coherence of every 8 Sep arm against the truth: coherent fraction by third octave from 6 kHz
for det on Hub EVAL12 is 0.050, 0.002, 0.002, 0.001, -0.000, 0.002 (the 5 % is the anti-aliasing
transition); every arm within +-0.003. det's kappa 0.06-0.12, so at least 88 % of the energy the spectral
loss puts above 6 kHz is uncorrelated with the truth. The implied deterministic SNR bound is 19.5 dB on
DataShare vs naive 19.20; no deterministic LISA trained in the project beats naive. Prediction (1) - the
ensemble mean has det's deficit - is false (-16.6 dB Hub, -10.0 dB DataShare).
hypothesis: The ensemble mean's deficit equals the deterministic model's and is a predictability spectrum; the deterministic deficit measures predictability.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-08-network-as-transport-map.md §1.2 (prediction 1, 'unpredictable at the waveform level') and §4.1; raw values in overnight2/analysis_OV2_es.json

title: Receptive-field test (LISASW, 22 ms context) - context does not make the high band coherent
content:
LISASW adds dilated residual convs (receptive field 263 input samples = 22 ms, +11k params) and trains the
paper loss and es_marg on the same batches for 26,000 steps. DataShare: coherent fraction above 7 kHz stays
0.000-0.005 for both; wide_det SNR 18.39 vs 18.35 (ceiling 19.5), LSD improves 0.03 via the envelope.
wide_es_marg is over-dispersed (+3.4 dB, SNR gap 4.46 vs calibrated 2.88). Hub: wide_det SNR 18.82 vs
18.86. Falsified: the 11-sample window is not why the band is unpredictable.
hypothesis: LISA's 11-sample (0.9 ms) receptive field is why the high band is incoherent; more context would make it predictable.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-08-network-as-transport-map.md §1.4 table and following paragraphs; overnight2/colab_results/results_OV2_wide.json

title: Hand-built stochastic rung S vs learned sampler on Hub EVAL12 - CRPS 0.753 vs 0.583
content:
The notebook's ladder (fitted on 200 training-speaker utterances) run on the 8 Sep det arm, same 12 Hub
utterances and CRPS definition. T1 quantile: HB-LSD 1.061, deficit -8.0 dB; T3: CRPS 0.982; S (noise
through the closed-form conditional map): CRPS 0.753; es_marg (noise through the learned map): CRPS 0.583,
a further 23 % off the rung. Controls behaved (mis-specified map 1.176 vs T0 1.097). Every rung except S is
strictly dominated by the learned sampler, and S is dominated on CRPS.
hypothesis: A network trained as the transport map beats the hand-built conditional transport rung on CRPS.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-08-network-as-transport-map.md §1.3 table; overnight2/colab_results/ladder_OV2_es_det.json

title: Graph toy - objective- vs architecture-induced over-smoothing separated by one sampler
content:
600-node 8-NN graph, unpredictable target component in modes >= 200. Shallow GNN + MSE loses 15.5 dB in
modes 200-400; the energy score restores it in one draw (-1.4 dB) and the ensemble mean reopens the hole
(-13.0 dB); a deep 8-layer no-skip GNN cannot restore it under any objective (-16.4 dB one draw). Second
experiment (per-node CRPS vs Euclidean vs sliced energy score) refuted the prediction that the joint
scores place noise in better bands: all three agree within a decibel.
hypothesis: Over-smoothing has an objective-induced cause independent of depth; a joint-proper score puts noise in the right graph-frequency bands where a marginal score does not.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-08-network-as-transport-map.md §2 table and §2.1 table; overnight2/gnn_toy_results.json

title: 8 Sep conditions judged by LSD + ViSQOL - speech-mode metrics blind to the band, passthrough fixes sampler
content:
29 conditions x 48 utterances re-scored. Speech-mode ViSQOL/PESQ cannot judge 12->48 kHz: on DataShare
naive upsampling scores best (ViSQOL-sp 4.245, PESQ 4.39). Audio-mode ViSQOL at 48 kHz rewards
deterministic high-band energy monotonically: winners are lambda=1e-1 on Hub (3.02, 46 % of the
empty-to-true range 1.57-4.73) and wide_det on DataShare. With baseband passthrough the sampler's
speech-ViSQOL penalty disappears (Hub one draw 3.06 -> 4.11) and its LSD beats det (0.933 vs 0.956): the
penalty was baseband leakage. No single model wins both CRPS and LSD+ViSQOL.
hypothesis: The sampler that wins CRPS also wins on the user's primary metrics LSD and ViSQOL.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-08-network-as-transport-map.md §7.1-§7.4 tables; overnight2/visqol_results/visqol_tables.md

title: OV3_fast - ERB-band energy score + logmean16 readout is the first arm to win both families
content:
7 arms x 16,000 steps, batch 64 x 1 s (7.6 epochs), EVAL12, M = 16, all with baseband passthrough.
es_erb_l0.1 read out as logmean16 scores CRPS 0.612, LSD 0.871, audio ViSQOL 2.773 (38.2 % of range) vs
det's 1.318 / 1.198 / 2.483: CRPS -53.6 %, LSD -27.3 %, +0.290 ViSQOL for -0.14 dB SNR. logmean16 improves
LSD for all six samplers (P7) but improves ViSQOL only for the two ERB arms: the readout must match the
aggregate the score is proper for. ERB arms are best calibrated (PIT end bins 0.211, kappa -0.009).
hypothesis: A score proper for the judge's own aggregate (log ERB-band energies), read out as the log-magnitude ensemble mean, improves CRPS, calibration, LSD and audio ViSQOL together.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-16-score-geometry-decoder-noise-readouts.md §3.1 scoreboard, §3.2 readout table, §3.3 calibration

title: OV3_fast negatives - higher spectral weight, low-band waveform term and decoder noise all refuted
content:
Four of seven pre-registered predictions refuted. P1: es_marg_l0.1 is worse than es_marg on LSD (1.004 vs
0.946), ViSQOL and CRPS (+15.5 %). P2: es_split_l0.1's deficit is larger (-15.18 vs -13.00 dB) - its noise
became decoration. P4: decoder noise leaves deficit at -10.79 dB; zeroing the decoder-noise draw moves
es_dec_erb_l0.1's output 74.7 dB below the signal, so trained LISASD models ignore their decoder noise.
P5: es_dec_erb_l0.1 is not the best arm. The geometry of the score was the lever, not the noise pathway.
hypothesis: P1 raising the spectral weight to 1e-1, P2 removing the waveform term above 6 kHz, P4 decoder-side noise each close the in-distribution energy gap.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-16-score-geometry-decoder-noise-readouts.md §2 predictions, §3.5 verdict table, §4 'Why decoder noise added nothing'

title: LISA's reported 24.16 dB is 3.16 dB above the task's ceiling and is scored on one batch of 8 s
content:
Under LISA's own Kaldi resampler, chunking and per-chunk-dB calc_snr on eight of its own held-out
speakers (391 chunks), the empty-high-band ceiling is 21.00 dB and naive sinc upsampling 20.67 dB; the
paper reports 24.16. eval_lisa.py scores only batch `ii == 3` (eight 1-s chunks); a sinc interpolator's
batch-to-batch sd is 3.63 dB and it scores >= 24.16 dB on 12.5 % of consecutive batches, against a claimed
4.75 dB margin over WSRGlow. Their LSD logs |X|^4 and pins 16.6 % of bins at the epsilon floor (2.213 vs
conventional 5.172 on the same signal). Aliasing hypothesis refuted: their downsampling is anti-aliased.
hypothesis: The paper's 24.16 dB comes from an SNR convention or down-sampling operator (e.g. aliased input), not from the model.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-17-lisa-reported-numbers-audit.md §0, §2 'Not aliasing', §3.3 table, §4 ceiling block, §5 batch block

title: SNR cannot rank models on 12->48 kHz - naive is the zero-recovery optimum to within 0.1 dB
content:
On 64 held-out utterances, SNR as a function of the coherently recovered high-band fraction: 0 % -> 19.11
dB, 2 % (this model class) -> 19.19, 10 % -> 19.56, 50 % -> 22.12; naive sinc measures 19.01. The whole
achievable range is about 1 dB on top of a 4.32 dB per-utterance spread, and every dB of incoherent high
band a model restores costs SNR (4 Sep lambda sweep: 19.16 / 18.37 / 17.69 as the deficit closes). SNR
retired as a ranking metric; report it only beside naive on the same audio.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-17-snr-ceiling-gating-and-scale.md §1 both tables; script audit/snr_scale.py

title: High band does not gate with speech (one utterance, es_erb_l0.1) - later corrected across 12 utterances
content:
On es_erb_l0.1 at step 13500, one utterance (p236_002): high-band energy ratio -11.68 dB on loud frames
and +0.99 dB on quiet frames, a 12.7 dB swing hidden by the mean deficit of -10.87 dB. Low-passing the
draw at 8 kHz buys 0.10 dB SNR and costs 25 dB of deficit, so the demo audio should not be low-passed.
The note read the gating as the sampler's defect; the 16 Sep note's 12-utterance, 7-arm measurement later
found every sampler gates better than det, correcting that reading.
hypothesis: The sampler's hiss comes from a high band that sits at a constant level instead of gating with the speech.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-17-snr-ceiling-gating-and-scale.md §2 low-pass table and §2.1 gating table; correction in notes/2026-09-16-score-geometry-decoder-noise-readouts.md §3.4

title: The deficit is a compressed envelope, and the envelope is 88 % predictable from the low band
content:
Regressing each OV3_fast arm's log high-band frame energy on the truth's (12 utterances, six held-out
speakers): slope below 1 for every arm (0.746-0.861) with r 0.86-0.93 - compressed variance, not wrong
assignment; the ERB term fixed the sd ratio (0.829 -> 0.996). On the truth alone, a 16-band low-band
profile predicts the 16 high ERB band energies with leave-one-speaker-out R^2 0.882. A fitted linear
rescale takes det past every sampler's raw LSD; a global per-band gain zeroes the mean deficit but adds
7 dB in the silences (a fraud detector). Fixing the envelope buys all of the deficit; fixing fine
structure buys 41 % of HB-LSD.
hypothesis: The loud/quiet deficit is compressed variance (regression to the mean one level up) rather than wrong assignment, and the high-band envelope is predictable from the low band.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-21-envelope-is-the-deficit.md §2 table, §3 block, §4 rescale table, §5 swap table

title: OV50 (50 epochs, 8 arms) - samplers halve the deficit but are not calibrated; ViSQOL edge gone
content:
Eight arms, 104,950 steps each on identical batches, evaluated on EVAL12 (CPU, converted checkpoints).
Best sampler es_dec_erb_l0.1: CRPS 0.5700 vs det 0.9597, deficit -6.85 vs -12.61 dB, logmean16+pt LSD
0.835 vs det 0.910, audio ViSQOL 3.021 vs det 3.001 (46.0 % vs 45.4 % of range). The 16 Sep ViSQOL margin
of 0.290 shrank to 0.020: det gained +0.518 with 6.5x more training. Calibration fails: PIT end bins 1.55x
ideal at best with all excess in the top bin (an energy bias), SNR gap 0.69-1.04 vs 2.75. det_paper
(LISA's lambda = 0) has deficit -27.63 dB. PESQ ranks det_paper and naive 2nd/3rd of 43 conditions.
hypothesis: At 50 epochs the ERB/decoder-noise samplers clear the 16 Sep rule: improve CRPS, calibration, LSD and audio ViSQOL together.

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-21-eval-results.md EVAL12 table, ViSQOL table, 'Against the 16 Sep run', 'Does the sampler programme clear its own bar?'; overnight3/results_OV50/table_OV50.md

title: Four released BWE models through one scorer - FLowHigh is a regressor, NU-Wave 2 samples 8-9 dB too quietly
content:
FLowHigh, AP-BWE, NU-Wave 2 and AudioSR, released weights and own inference code, scored on the
NU-Wave 2/FLowHigh test speakers (240 utterances for levels/LSD/ViSQOL, 32 x 8 draws for calibration).
FLowHigh ranks first on LSD/ViSQOL (0.761/3.61) yet its 8-draw gap is 0.08 dB against 1.77 for
independent draws at its level: one Euler step returns the conditional mean. NU-Wave 2 deficit -7.96 dB;
AudioSR biased by band, gap 2.62 vs 3.92. Our 88k sampler: deficit -0.70 dB, fair CRPS 0.514. Empty-band
SNR ceiling 22.02 dB at 12 kHz; every model has coherent fraction below 0.02.
hypothesis: Released generative BWE models are not calibrated samplers of the missing band; single-reference metrics cannot tell a sampler from a regressor.

extraction.evidence: paper/main.tex Setup, 'Level Before Dispersion', Table 1 (tab:released), 'What the Audit Finds'

title: Pre-registered ENV arms - context + per-frame HB log-energy score should stop level regressing per utterance
content:
After the SOTA audit found each utterance's level regressing toward the corpus mean (over 270 utterances
es_dec_erb_l0.1 r = -0.41, slope -0.29 dB per dB; det r = -0.42), predictions were written before
training ENV arms (fast/arms_env.py, fast/train_env.py): P5 es_ctx_env_l0.1 lifts the deficit's
correlation with the utterance's HB share above -0.2 and closes loud-frame deficits on p236/p238 to better
than -3 dB; P6 context moves it more than the objective; P7 neither changes the coherent fraction (stays
below 0.03). No results are recorded in the repo.
hypothesis: A 22 ms context plus a per-frame high-band log-energy energy score fixes per-utterance level regression (P5); context matters more than the objective (P6); coherent fraction stays below 0.03 (P7).

extraction.evidence: notes/2026-09-26-sota-diagnosis.md section 'The residual: level regresses per utterance', bullets P5-P7

title: Post-hoc transport ladder superseded by the learned sampler - a map on a point prediction is still a point
content:
The original programme corrected LISA's high-band deficit after training with transport maps T0-T4 and a
stochastic rung S. On an honest source T1 moved HB-LSD by 1.7 % and S moved CRPS by 21 %; the LISAS
sampler trained under the energy score moved CRPS by 43 % and dominates every rung. The notebook is kept
for three surviving lessons: LSD rewards regression to the log-domain mean, gates before data, and
adversarial controls (shaped noise, mis-specified map, frame shuffle) that caught LSD rewarding energy
inflation.
hypothesis: Optimal-transport maps on low-order high-band statistics can correct regression to the mean after training.

extraction.evidence: README.md section 'The earlier programme: post-hoc transport maps (superseded)'

title: LSD structurally rewards regression to the log-domain mean and is never trusted alone
content:
A perfect sampler scores ~2x worse in expected squared error than the conditional-mean predictor, so LSD
ranks samplers below point predictors by construction. Evidence across the repo: the broken lambda=1.0
model beat the correct one on LSD, a mis-specified map beat shaped noise on HB-LSD, and LISA (89k,
deterministic) reports LSD 0.81 against WSRGlow's 1.01, partly because LISA's LSD code logs |X|^4 and pins
16.6 % of the spectrogram at its epsilon floor. Band-energy ratio measures the disease, CRPS the cure; LSD
is reported but not compared across papers.
hypothesis: H4: LSD rewards energy matching / regression to the log-domain mean and must not be primary evidence.

extraction.evidence: README.md numbered item 1 under 'The earlier programme'; detail in notes/2026-09-01 §3 and notes/2026-09-17-lisa-reported-numbers-audit.md §3.3

title: Hub and DataShare held-out sets disagree by 5-8 dB on the same checkpoint - provenance unresolved
content:
The same checkpoint measures a high-band deficit 5-8 dB deeper on the Hub test_utts than on the DataShare
test_FULL.npz for the same speakers (both mic1); the 8 Sep sampler is energy-calibrated on one and
under-dispersed on the other. Until provenance is settled every number must name its set. The DataShare
fetch URL also returns 403, so the cache cannot be rebuilt from the notebook. Open TODO.
